## 6. Function

Implement exactly this behaviour (from the reference program's documentation):

```text
Python prototype of the edge- and motion-based object
  detectors planned for video_processor, written as an integer model of
  the hardware (feature_detect + object_tracker run filter and blobs) and
  of the firmware (shape checks, multi-target tracking), so its numbers
  carry over to the RTL. Per input GIF it writes, next to this script:
    <name>_proto.gif     the frames with the tracking boxes (class colours,
                         pedestrians / faces dashed boxes, vehicles a solid
                         box in the middle)
    <name>_features.gif  the feature bits: edge red, motion green, both
                         yellow, over the darkened frame
    <name>_sheet.png     contact sheet of the tracked frames
    <name>_log.txt       per frame: global shift, blobs, targets
  Features (one per pixel, computed once for every detector):
    edge    3 x 3 Sobel on luma Y = (R + 2G + B) / 4, |Gx| + |Gy| >
            EDGE_T; then "an edge within the last EDGE_SPAN pixels of the
            line" (fills textured objects into runs)
    motion  background of CELL x CELL cells: per cell the lowest and
            highest luma (each moved towards the frame's by 1 / 2^BG_RATE
            per frame); a pixel outside [min - MOT_T, max + MOT_T] of its
            cell (read at the camera's shift) moves; filled like edges.
            The shift between frames comes from the column / row luma
            profiles (sum of absolute differences, +- SHIFT_MAX cells).
  The prototype works on the GIF frames as the camera sends them (no ISP
  demosaic or blur), so absolute thresholds may move a little in RTL.
  Camera videos (MP4, MOV, MKV, WebM) are read with the testbench's
  tb/scripts/mp4_io.py (PyAV): sampled at --fps from --start, at most
  --video-frames frames, fitted to 320 x 240 the same way run_sim.sh does.
  Without inputs: every GIF and video of tb/images.
```

Per function:

```text
native_fit: The fit box of an input at its native size, capped (cap for landscape, turned for portrait).

load: GIF frames at the tracking size (fit inside fit = (w, h), 320 x 240 by default as the SV testbench;
None: the native size up to 1920 x 1080 / 1080 x 1920; width multiple of 4, even height,
nearest-neighbour as gif_io), as uint8 H x W x 3 RGB; a video through mp4_io (as run_sim.sh).

fill: A set bit in the last span pixels of the line (the hardware's run-fill counter).

edges: Edge bit of pixel (x, y): the 3 x 3 Sobel magnitude |Gx| + |Gy| of the window centred on
(x - 1, y - 1) (the hardware streams: rows y - 2 .. y, columns x - 2 .. x) above EDGE_T; 0 for
x < 2 or y < 2. Then filled along the line (an edge in the last EDGE_SPAN pixels).

skin_table: The learned skin table (32 x 32 bits over the window SKIN_CB0 / SKIN_CR0, 2 steps per cell), or None.

fixed_skin: The fixed skin rule (iteration 1) on a feature dict (y, cb, cr, sat, r, g, b arrays).

profiles: Per class (the firmware's detector set-up): term A = the luma / colour test combined with the
motion bit, its run band; term B = the edge bit and its run band (or none); blob gaps (columns,
lines; vehicles 12: roof and body apart at the windows) and least pixels.

term_runs: Counted runs of one detector term: (y, closing column, term, x0, x1); a run is judged by its
whole length when it closes (at the pixel after it, or its last pixel at the end of the line).

runs_blobs: object_tracker: the counted runs grouped into NBLOB blob slots in one pass; with term B on,
term A's runs use slots 0 .. NBLOB/2 - 1 and term B's the others (the two never join); the blobs of
at least keep pixels, in slot order.

face_segments: The blob split into vertical segments (each a blob of its rows): at rows without skin and at
waists, a row narrower than WAIST of the widest row above it and of the widest below it (a neck, or
a skin-coloured wall joined to a head); each segment is a face candidate (then face_cut).

face_cut: A face blob without its neck and shoulders: rows from the top until one is narrower than
NECK of the widest so far (once the face is FACE_HMIN of that width tall), at most FACE_HMAX of
it tall. Returns the blob (x0, x1, y0, y1, n, runs) of the kept rows.

face_upright: Not an arm: the centres of the blob's rows drift at most ARM_DRIFT pixels per row from the top
row to the bottom one (a forearm crosses its box diagonally).

face_eyes: A face EYES_W or wider: a dark non-skin pixel in each half of the eye band (two eyes).

face_structure: A face, not a hand or a skin-coloured patch: hair above it (HAIR_FRAC of the band above
darker than the face) or eyes / mouth inside (FEAT_FRAC of the inner band not skin and darker).

draw_label: Number n in the 3 x 5 overlay font beside the box (right side, left when no room), on a dark
backdrop.

zoom_video: --zoom: the tracked video, then a slow zoom onto face number z['face'] once it has been tracked
z['after'] frames in a row, over z['time'] seconds (ease in and out, following the face); the zoom
reads the face from the source at its full resolution (a video: the decoded frames up to 1280
pixels, not the 320 x 240 tracking frames) and enhances it (contrast stretch, sharpening, stronger
as it zooms in); the fully zoomed face is the last frame, held z['hold'] seconds.
Writes <name>_zoom<N>.gif and .mp4, z['scale'] times the tracking frame size.

sheet: Contact sheet of up to 24 frames, 6 across, each scaled (nearest) by scale, at most tile_max wide.

Motion: feature_detect's motion bit. Background: per CELL x CELL cell the lowest and highest luma
(4 fraction bits), two banks (one read during the frame, the other written; they swap at the frame
end). Pixel (x, y) in cell (cx, cy) moves when the background is valid and the cell it came from,
(cx - sx, cy - sy) with the shift (sx, sy) in effect, is in the frame, and its luma is below
lo - MOT_T or above hi + MOT_T (integer parts); filled along the line. At the frame end every cell
becomes old + (new - old) >> BG_RATE (arithmetic shift) of its source cell, or the new min / max
when there is none; the column / row luma profiles (sums per cell column / row) are compared with
the previous frame's: the shift s in -SHIFT_MAX .. SHIFT_MAX with the lowest sum over the middle
entries (i = SHIFT_MAX .. n - 1 - SHIFT_MAX) of |cur[i] - prev[i - s]| (s = 0 kept on a tie)
applies to the next frame.
```

## 6a. Industry reference check

Comparison of section 6 with published engineering references. Every difference is a `TODO(REF-...)` written as a prompt for updating the program.

```text
// Industry reference check - detect_proto.py (2026-10-16)
// Sources:
//   [1] D. Chai, K. N. Ngan, "Face segmentation using skin-color map in videophone
//   applications", IEEE TCSVT 9(4):551-564, 1999, https://webarchive.lib.cuhk.edu.hk/2021032815
//   4327mp_/http:/www.ee.cuhk.edu.hk/~knngan/TCSVT_v9_n4_p551-564.pdf (skin map Cb 77-127, Cr
//   133-173 in BT.601 YCbCr)
//   [2] ITU-R BT.601-7 (2011) https://www.itu.int/rec/R-REC-BT.601 and BT.709-6 (2015)
//   https://www.itu.int/rec/R-REC-BT.709 - Kr/Kb 0.299/0.114 and 0.2126/0.0722, 8-bit Y = 16 +
//   219 E'Y, C = 128 + 224 E'C; scaled equations in Linux V4L2 colorspaces
//   https://docs.kernel.org/7.1/_sources/userspace-api/media/v4l/colorspaces-details.rst.txt
//   [3] I. Haritaoglu, D. Harwood, L. S. Davis, "W4: Real-time surveillance of people and their
//   activities", IEEE PAMI 22(8), 2000, doi:10.1109/34.868683 (background as per-pixel minimum
//   / maximum intensity, foreground outside it)
//   [4] D. G. Bailey, C. T. Johnston, "Single pass connected components analysis", IVCNZ 2007;
//   N. Ma, D. G. Bailey, C. T. Johnston, "Optimised single pass connected components analysis",
//   FPT 2008, https://sfat.massey.ac.nz/research/centres/crisp/pdfs/2008_FPT_185.pdf; MathWorks
//   Vision HDL blob analysis https://www.mathworks.com/help/visionhdl/ug/blob-analysis.html
//   [5] P. R. Kalata, "The Tracking Index: A Generalized Parameter for alpha-beta and alpha-
//   beta-gamma Target Trackers", IEEE Trans. AES 20(2):174-182, 1984; summary
//   https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alpha_beta_filter (x_p = x + v T; r = z - x_p; x += alpha r;
//   v += beta r / T)
// Published algorithm / rules:
//   Prototype of the hardware detectors and firmware tracking. Skin colour: Chai & Ngan Cb
//   77-127, Cr 133-173 in BT.601 YCbCr (Cb = 128 + 0.564 (B - Y), Y = 0.299 R + 0.587 G + 0.114
//   B).
// Comparison with this program (section 6):
//   Mirrors the hardware exactly (luma (R + 2G + B) / 4, chroma (B - Y) / 2, run / blob
//   grouping, W4-style motion), as a model must. Differs from the reference: the skin window
//   (Cb 77-127, Cr 135-175) is Chai & Ngan's BT.601 window applied to the approximate chroma,
//   whose scale is 0.5 instead of 0.564 / 0.713, so the window is shifted relative to the
//   published one (the learned skin table compensates when used).
// RESOLVED(REF-DETECT_PROTO-1) [LOW] Skin window in the approximate colour space. Resolution:
//   2026-10-16: the fixed rule is documented as Chai & Ngan's window in the approximate chroma;
//   the learned table (SKIN_LUT) stays the default.
```
